display.purpose: The scores and the clock, and nothing else. Always through the `.nums` class (tabular figures, -0.02em).

headline.purpose: A screen's title, once per page.

title.purpose: A card's or a section's title, often uppercase.

body.purpose: All the ordinary content. By far the most used size in the repo.

label.purpose: “FAUTES”, “PROCHAINE ÉCHÉANCE”. It is this size that gives the “match sheet” grain.

body-compact.purpose: The body of dialogs and dense secondary panels (a confirmation's message, a code dialog, an administration hint, the access panel), plus a few tight controls. A dialog is read close up on a narrow surface: one step under the ordinary body holds the measure there without shrinking the target.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The invariant. Depth is tonal: the staircase of six neutral planes plus a 1 px hairline. Towards black, a black shadow has nothing left to darken, and Tailwind's shadows read as a smudge on the light banner.

shadows.name: shell
shadows.purpose: The one exception, and it is a shadow of staging rather than of depth: above 1024 px it detaches the rounded shell from its gutter, like a sheet laid on a desk.

motion.name: exponential-out
motion.purpose: The product's only curve. A clean exit from an already visible state.

motion.name: score-up
motion.purpose: The score rises because someone scored: it arrives growing into its place.

motion.name: score-down
motion.purpose: The score falls because someone undid: it starts larger and withdraws. The direction carries the cause — the same motion in both cases would say “something changed” where you need to read “what”.

motion.name: bonus-in
motion.purpose: The Bonus pill on mount, once: on the fifth team foul (TEAM_FOUL_BONUS, five under FFBB rules), it is the game's rule that changes.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion, infinite loops stop at full opacity and the score's motion becomes a flash — the acknowledgement survives, only the travel disappears.

components.name: Primary button
components.description: The screen's action. Lemon flat area, near-black ink, a finger tall.

components.name: Neutral button

narrative.overview:
A gym in the evening. The hall is dark, and what gives light is the scoreboard and the court's lines. Swish is that scene: a near-black ink canvas, and a single electric lemon carrying everything that counts — the opposition's score, the button about to be touched, the current period. Colour is rare because it is light, and a hall with ten lamps lights nothing.

The product is a tool, not a showcase. It is held one-handed in a gym, under a thumb, while a game is being played — and it is also read from a distance, projected for spectators. The numbers are therefore the main object: tabular, very heavy, enormous when they are the score. Everything else recedes behind them.

The world is dark first, and that is a choice of identity, not an economy mode. The light theme exists and it is composed, never inherited. Three palettes were rejected before this one, all for the same reason — they derived every colour from a contrast constraint against white, which forces darkening and desaturation.
keyCharacteristics: Ink canvas, a single electric lemon accent (#dcff33)
Tabular figures, weights 800–900, up to 6 rem for a score
No shadow: depth comes from a staircase of planes and a 1 px hairline
Every control is 44 px tall, without exception
Two themes composed separately, neither derived from the other
The playbook court has its own palette, whose colour convention does not switch

rules.name: The fill rule
rules.body: Colour lives in the flat areas, with their paired ink (*-fill + on-*); the inks stay near-black or near-white. A colour that does not have to read as small text on white no longer needs darkening — and it was the darkening that made the whole thing drab. Corollary: brand fills, accent writes.

rules.name: The one-voice rule
rules.body: One accent across the whole application. A second accent does not double the expressiveness, it halves the legibility of the first.

rules.name: The desk rule
rules.body: The gutter must be visible and must never dominate the card. The direction of the gap follows the room available: on light there is room under the paper, on dark there is none under the black.

rules.name: The hash rule
rules.body: A colour drawn from a hash of an id is right for a crest in a list, and wrong everywhere else. Never as ink, nor as a chart series.

rules.name: The tabular-figures rule
rules.body: Every number that can change under the eye carries .nums. A score going from 9 to 10 must not shift what surrounds it.

rules.name: The three-small-sizes rule
rules.body: The scale of small sizes stops at three steps — 12 px for the label, 13 px for the dialog, 14 px for the content — and each has a surface of its own. A fourth step would add no hierarchy, it would add a hesitation: beyond that we distinguish by weight and case. First written as “the two-sizes rule”, forbidding the 13 px step, it was an invention — the repo uses it nineteen times across ten files, consistently.

rules.name: The finger rule
rules.body: Every control is 44 px tall at minimum, and 24 px is the absolute floor even under a pointer. Below sm, an action never shares its row with text.

rules.name: The plane rule
rules.body: An element detaches by its plane and its hairline, never by a shadow. If two surfaces do not separate, spread their lightnesses. And never veil a card with opacity.

rules.name: The top-hairline rule
rules.body: A panel belonging to a team carries a 3 px inner rule in the brand colour along its top edge, and nothing else.

dos: Do let colour be carried by a flat area with its paired ink (--c-*-fill + --c-on-*).
Do use --c-brand to fill and --c-accent to write.
Do give every control 44 px of height, and move the action under the text below sm.
Do point the shadcn tokens (--card, --muted, --background) at the --c-* planes.
Do carry .nums on every number liable to change under the eye.
Do compose the light theme separately. It is not derived from the dark one.
Do check both themes before concluding. Dark forgives lemon everywhere; light does not.
donts: Don't add a shadow to detach an element. Spread the planes, lay a 1 px hairline.
Don't veil a card (bg-card/50): the veil cancels half the separation of the planes.
Don't use a raw Tailwind colour (bg-red-600, text-emerald-700). The repo contains none.
Don't create a token family for a surface that “would not switch”. It was tried twice and both produced a black rectangle in the middle of a light application.
Don't colour a text or a chart series by a hash of an id.
Don't put a field's name in its placeholder alone.
Don't announce a contrast ratio in a comment; they live in src/ui/theme/contrast.test.ts.
Don't add motion to make the finish visible.
